summary: The focused obligation is necessary. The old harness cannot call cJSON_Minify on a whole-input single-line comment in either version because it returns when parsing produces no JSON value.

claims.necessity_reason: Minification is an entry operation. The finite input 1000//\n\0 passes the entry checks. cJSON_Minify can remove its entire comment body, leaving an empty string, but the parse-success gate prevents that call. A parsed JSON value cannot yield the same empty whole-input result.

before.requirement: Allow cJSON_Minify to reduce a whole-input single-line comment to an empty string.
before.reason: Minify consumes the comment and newline. The comment-only body supplies no JSON value, so parsing returns NULL and the harness exits before Minify.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Consumes the single-line comment through its newline.
Routes the harness's parse call to the length-aware parser.
A failed value parse returns no item.
The complete value dispatch has no case for the comment-only body.

after.requirement: Allow cJSON_Minify to reduce a whole-input single-line comment to an empty string.
after.reason: The same Minify behavior remains supported. The unchanged parse-success gate still prevents the call on a comment-only body.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Consumes the single-line comment through its newline.
Routes the harness's parse call to the length-aware parser.
A failed value parse still returns no item.
The complete value dispatch still has no case for the comment-only body.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The only Minify call follows the parse-success check.

claims.comparison_reason: Both versions support the same whole-input comment removal. The same old-harness parse gate blocks it on both sides.
